body.statement: Suppose explicitly that \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), and suppose \(Y_u(a,e')\) is constant in \(e'\). For the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix reduction, let \(\mathcal{G}=\{\Omega\}\) be one complete-randomization cell with a fixed treatment count, require \(\pi\) to be exchangeable under every unit permutation on that cell, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)=\pi(\cdot)\). Condition on a unit permutation sampled independently of \(X\), use it as the fixed deterministic tie order \(\prec\), choose any nondecreasing \(\phi\), and set \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\), where \(T_{\mathrm C}(x,y)=\sum_{u\in U}Z_u(x)\phi(R_u(y))\). Then the bounded-null test reduces to their quantile-null randomization test, Theorem 4 gives the individual \(1-\alpha\) confidence set for each fixed \(\tau_{(k)}(e)\), and Section 5.5 gives the joint simultaneous construction over all effect quantiles. For the Su--Li reduction, let \(\mathcal{U}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_S\}\) be fixed, require \(\pi\) to be a product of mutually independent within-stratum complete-randomization laws with fixed treated counts and exchangeability within every \(U_s\), let \(\mathcal{G}\) be the corresponding partition into fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\). Condition on independently predeclared within-stratum unit permutations as the deterministic tie orders \(\prec_s\), choose every \(\phi_s\) nondecreasing, and set \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\), where \(T_{\mathrm S}(x,y)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{u\in U_s}Z_u(x)\phi_s(R_{su}(y))\). Then the bounded-null optimization is exactly their multiple-choice-knapsack problem and its simultaneous confidence-set inversion.
body.justification: The reduction checks that the new target respects the established no-interference boundary.
body.gap: The comparator results cover precisely these special cases rather than assignment-coupled network fibers.
body.consumer: Implementations can reuse verified no-interference routines whenever the legal relation collapses to partitions.
